title: Yosef Rishba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Shabbat 130a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.130a.10), Levi happened to visit the household of Yosef Rishba. They served him a peacock’s head in milk, but he did not eat. When he (Levi) came before Rabbi, Rabbi asked him: “Why did you not excommunicate them?” He replied: “It was the place of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,” etc.[^1] In [Chullin 54a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.54a), the household of Yosef Rishba struck (the animal) on the sciatic nerve and killed it; they came before R' Yehuda ben Beteira, etc.[^2]

notes.text: Hyman’s supplied text reads טוותא. The checked Shabbat passage reads טווסא, and the William Davidson Edition’s English translation explicitly renders it “peacock.” The context discusses birds’ meat in milk. “Peacock’s head” therefore replaces the earlier draft’s unsupported “lamb (roasted)” and the held untranslated form, without changing the Hebrew source. Rashi’s Vilna Edition gloss on רישבא is ציד עופות, “bird hunter”; it supports that descriptive name but does not itself gloss טווסא. Neither a new printed-page reading nor an external identity is claimed.

The Chullin passage was not included in this bounded source check and remains an unverified reference here. גידא נשיא is rendered conventionally as the sciatic nerve; the parenthetical animal is Hyman’s. The personal name in ר״י בן בתירא is expanded contextually from Yehuda ben Beteira earlier in the same notice; the Chullin occurrence’s title remains R' because that passage was not checked. Printed locators קל. and נד. are conventionally 130a and 54a. Hyman’s “etc.” is retained without adding the remainder of the checked Shabbat discussion.

In the checked William Davidson Hebrew paragraph of Shabbat 130a:10, the cited locality explicitly has דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה. That full title supports this Shabbat occurrence only. Hyman’s bare דרבי is retained as Rabbi without adding a personal name; the unverified Chullin title is not inferred from the Shabbat title.
